chart.title: Gender of the chief executive
chart.subtitle: "Chief executive" is defined here as the head of state or the head of government, whoever has more power over the appointment and dismissal of cabinet ministers.
chart.note: This is recorded on December 31 of each year. When the head of state and head of government hold equal power, the head of government is considered the chief executive.

Woman chief executive (31st December).descriptionShort: The variable denotes whether the chief executive of government in office on December 31 is a woman.
Woman chief executive (31st December).descriptionProcessing:
Assigns the value based on the gender of the most powerful chief: either Head of state or Head of government.

Uses gender from HOS:
  - If head of state is more powerful than head of government, and head of state is the head of the executive.
  - If head of state is also head of government.
  - If head of government is less powerful than head of state.

Uses HOG if:
  - If head of state is less powerful than head of government

We derive this indicator from V-Dem indicators: `v2exfemhos`, `v2exfemhog`, `v2ex_hosw`, and `v2ex_hogw`.

### Data imputation
Unlike most indicators in this dataset, this one is not extended back in time with the data of the historical entity a country was part of. Who led a country is a fact about that country rather than about the power that ruled its territory earlier, so the years before a country appears in V-Dem's data are left empty.
